title: Postnatal maternal red flags
summary: Recognising when a postnatal woman needs urgent review rather than routine postnatal care.
redFlags: Heavy bleeding or other signs of postpartum haemorrhage.
Fever, rigors, or other signs of sepsis.
Severe headache, visual disturbance, or very high blood pressure — late-onset pre-eclampsia can present after birth.
Calf swelling/pain or breathlessness/chest pain — venous thromboembolism risk is raised throughout the 6 weeks postpartum.
Severe or worsening abdominal pain, or wound breakdown/infection signs.
Significant, rapid deterioration in mood, thinking, or behaviour.

blocks.heading: Heavy bleeding
bullets: See the Major obstetric haemorrhage emergency drill — postpartum haemorrhage can occur at any point in the puerperium, not only immediately after birth.

blocks.heading: Fever or signs of sepsis
bullets: See the Suspected maternal sepsis emergency drill.
Common postnatal sources include endometritis, wound/perineal infection, mastitis, and urinary tract infection.

blocks.heading: Headache, visual disturbance, or raised BP
bullets: Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia can present for the first time, or worsen, after birth — work through the Headache, visual disturbance or epigastric pain topic for BP-banded guidance; see the Eclampsia emergency drill if any seizure activity occurs.

blocks.heading: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) awareness
bullets: Pregnancy and the 6 weeks after birth are a higher-risk period for VTE.
Ask specifically about calf pain, swelling, redness, chest pain, or breathlessness — escalate urgently if suspected rather than waiting to see if it settles.
VERIFY local VTE risk-assessment tool and thresholds for thromboprophylaxis.

blocks.heading: Routine postnatal observations
bullets: General principle — VERIFY local observation schedule: temperature, pulse, blood pressure, lochia (amount, colour, odour), uterine involution, perineal/wound healing, mood, and infant feeding.
Ask specifically about each red flag above at every postnatal contact, not only if volunteered.

citations.section: Postnatal care — recognising and responding to maternal red-flag symptoms
Maternal mortality reports — VTE and sepsis as leading causes of late maternal death, delayed recognition as a preventable factor
